newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Telecoms win would boost Inparsa.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms win would boost Inparsa.

text.p: The next price target for shares in tourism-to-industrial group Inparsa is 4,000 escudos and the stock could climb to 5,000 if it wins bidding to operate Portugal's third cellular phone licence, analysts say.

Inparsa shares hit a high of 3,598 escudos, up 645, in volume of 488,040 at 1413 GMT. The shares have more than doubled since Inparsa was created following the restructuring of Sonae Investimentos, part of the Sonae group, earlier this year.

The recent rise of the stock is also linked to Inparsa's recent acquisition of tourism group Torralta, revenue from the sale of tourism concern Orbitur, and a shortage of stock as only 28 percent of Inparsa has been floated.
"I think that if Inparsa wins its bid for the third mobile phone licence, the share could go to 5,000 escudos," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Another said: "Right now, Inparsa is rising because of speculation, discounting a number of things, including profits for the coming years and victory in the bidding for the new mobile phone licence."
So far, just one group, a consortium including Inparsa, state-run utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, Maxitel, Transgas and Gas de Portugal, has said it will bid jointly for the licence.
Candidates must present bids by September 15 and a decision will be taken by the end of 1997.

"Inparsa incorporates a number of factors that permit the stock to rise sustainedly while the rest of the market is weak. It sold Orbitur, which was a lame duck, and took a profit of about two billion escudos, and its recent acquisition Torralta has good prospects, as does its telecommunications venture," said one dealer.
